---
name: brainstorming
description: "Use for open-ended feature or design work with unresolved requirements or consequential choices."
---

# Resolve the design

Read the relevant code and constraints, identify the desired outcome, and separate established decisions from missing requirements. Reuse the existing design when it meets the request.

For routine reversible choices, state a reasonable assumption and proceed with authorized work. Ask a focused question when an unresolved choice changes scope, public behavior, data safety, or a user-selected design. Work on independent parts while awaiting the answer. A request for design only remains design only.

Compare alternatives only when a real tradeoff matters. Describe the chosen behavior, affected boundaries, failure handling, and verification at the depth needed to implement it. For substantial design work, save a concise design in the project's documentation location; do not duplicate full implementation code in it.

Once the user has authorized implementation and the design is sufficiently determined, continue without another approval ritual. Commit or publish only when authorized. Use writing-plans when the remaining work needs a durable multi-step plan. Use an existing visualization tool when a visual helps resolve a concrete design question; do not automatically start a companion server.
